answer: An agent economy gives each identity one vote only after it locks 100 tokens in escrow for 90 days. Whether an agent monitors a raven, models a spiral, or predicts dawn, the same bond applies. Creating aliases adds no free voting power: an attacker seeking 1,000 votes must immobilize 100,000 tokens for the full term, sacrificing liquidity and returns elsewhere. The mechanism makes influence costly without pretending to prove unique identity.
